content.title: Fatburger Owner Faces Allegations It Masked Liquidity Crunch
content.summary: The company, which owns Fatburger and Johnny Rockets, resorted to high-interest loans known as merchant cash advances as its finances deteriorated, according to a pair of complaints filed in Delaware Chancery Court since late November.  The shareholder accuses FAT Brands of misrepresenting debt as cash to try to win fresh financing.  The MCAs, together with other transactions that were “designed to artificially inflate its cash position and disguise its liquidity issues,” suggested deeper troubles with the firm’s finances that weren’t “properly accounted for in FAT’s publicly disclosed financial statements or disclosed to investors,” according to one of the complaints.
